name: Learn proper knife technique
blurb: The grip, the claw and the rocking motion. Good knife skills make cooking faster, safer and more pleasant, and they are almost entirely a matter of practising a few fixed motions.
gear: A stable board on a damp cloth
steps: Learn the pinch grip: thumb and forefinger on the blade itself, just ahead of the handle. This gives control the handle-only grip cannot.
Learn the claw with your guiding hand: fingertips curled under, knuckles against the blade as a guide, so the knife physically cannot reach your fingertips.
Learn the rock chop: the tip stays in contact with the board while the heel rises and falls.
Learn to slice with a drawing motion rather than pressing down — a sharp knife should not need force.
Learn the standard cuts: julienne, dice, brunoise, chiffonade, and practise on a bag of carrots.
Practise for speed only after the motion is correct and safe.
tips: A dull knife causes most kitchen cuts because it slips instead of biting.
Stabilise the board with a damp cloth underneath. A moving board is genuinely dangerous.
Never try to catch a falling knife. Step back and let it land.
proof: You dice a full mirepoix with even pieces, correct grip and claw, without looking at your hands the whole time.
